gotchas.text: Tool calling needs SGLang with the minicpm5 tool-call parser (sgl-project/sglang#25600). The openbmb cookbook says to install SGLang from main because v0.5.12.post1 lacked it; the PyPI 0.5.20 wheel used here ships it, so no source build is needed any more. The model writes XML tool calls (<function name="x"><param name="k">v</param></function>) and they come back as OpenAI tool_calls with finish_reason tool_calls, with thinking on and off.

SGLang has no MiniCPM5 reasoning parser, but the model uses plain <think> ... </think>, so --reasoning-parser qwen3 splits it into reasoning_content. With enable_thinking left unset the template adds no <think> prefix; the model opens the tag itself and the qwen3 parser still catches it.

flashinfer JIT-compiles its prefill kernels on the first request and shells out to ninja. In a venv that is not activated the first prefill dies with FileNotFoundError: ninja and the scheduler exits; put the venv bin directory on PATH before starting the server.
In a llama.cpp deployment the card warns that the default min_p 0.05 causes repetition and asks for min_p 0; the SGLang default min_p is already 0.

Accuracy here is far below the same suite with thinking left on, and the gap was checked by hand before it was reported: it is a real loss, not a format or scorer artefact. Every miss inspected came back as a clean extracted answer in exactly the shape the suite expects - a bare option letter for the syllogism items, a bare name for the ordering items - two or three output tokens long, with nothing wrapped in tags and nothing stranded in reasoning_content. The model simply answers immediately and guesses. The same items, with thinking on, took 558-1,555 output tokens and came out right.

Thinking OFF row. On MiniCPM5 that means the chat template was rendered with enable_thinking=false, which prefills an empty think block instead of opening <think>; it goes out as chat_template_kwargs {"enable_thinking": false} on every request of the run and is recorded in this row's request block, which is why this row does not share its config_id with the thinking-on row of the pair. Nothing else differs: same server, same flags, temperature 0 and seed 42. The row exists because more than 10 % of the thinking-on row's items ran into the output budget: 51 of its 120 items hit the 2,048-token cap mid-thought, which scores them wrong however good the model is. Here that is 10 of 120, and accuracy moves 0.5083 -> 0.1917. The per-item spot-check behind that direction is the gotcha alongside this one. Read the pair together, never this row alone, and do not compare this number with a model that has no thinking mode to turn off.

provenance.notes: Weights: openbmb/MiniCPM5-1B at 87179e5c1f455ef22e6223592d2d61351b525bfc, BF16, one 2.16 GB safetensors shard, sha256 checked against the Hub. SGLang 0.5.20 from PyPI in a Python 3.12 venv (uv) with torch 2.13.0+cu130, flashinfer-python 0.6.18, sglang-kernel 0.4.7, triton 3.7.1, transformers 5.12.1, xgrammar 0.2.1; CUDA 13.0, driver 580.173.02, Ubuntu 24.04.4, kernel 6.17.0-1029-nvidia. Environment SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1 and SGLANG_DISABLE_CUDNN_CHECK=1 as the MiniCPM SGLang cookbook recommends, the venv bin directory on PATH (flashinfer JIT needs ninja). Server flags follow the openbmb SGLang cookbook (docs/deployment/sglang.md): --dtype bfloat16 --context-length 131072 --tool-call-parser minicpm5, plus --reasoning-parser qwen3 so the <think> block lands in reasoning_content; --mem-fraction-static 0.75 instead of the cookbook 0.85 to leave the unified-memory box about 20 GB of host headroom (the KV pool still holds about 2 million tokens). Radix prefix cache, chunked prefill 8192, CUDA graphs and the flashinfer attention backend are SGLang defaults. Every request sets temperature 0 and seed 42 as the workloads specify. The chat template has three thinking states: enable_thinking true prefills <think>, false prefills an empty think block, and unset lets the model decide, which on almost every prompt means it thinks. Speed and long-context depth rows send chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking false; eval and needle rows leave it unset (the template default). Load: weights 13.0 s (2.38 GB), KV cache allocation 3.2 s, CUDA graph capture 10.6 s, scheduler end to end 32.2 s; SGLang reported max_total_num_tokens 3,679,002 and chunked_prefill_size 8192, and 23.5 GB of GPU memory was still free after start. max_running_requests is passed explicitly as 512 (the SGLang default on this box was 4096) so the concurrency limit is recorded in the row args and can be read back from /get_server_info; it was confirmed at 512 on this server before the first concurrent row. Thinking OFF row. MiniCPM5 thinks by default, and on this suite more than 10 % of the items ran into the output-token budget mid-thought, which scores them wrong however good the model is. This row repeats the same suite with chat_template_kwargs {"enable_thinking": false} and everything else identical; the default-thinking row is kept alongside it, and the pair is the measurement. Accuracy here is not comparable to a model that has no thinking mode to turn off.
